objective: Proof. Assemble: parity's count is polynomial; the clause and not-all-equal never fail; every other class except the five weak ones builds a link and is NP-complete on 4-regular systems. So, unless NP-complete problems are polynomial, a mutually selecting four-place knot would have to be one of the five weak classes, which never failed in any search.
status: Proved by FOUR-PREFER-20261101-001D-P001: of the 20 four-place knot classes, 15 are settled and none is mutually selecting unless NP-complete problems are polynomial (parity's count is polynomial; the clause and not-all-equal never fail; twelve classes are NP-complete on 4-regular systems); a mutually selecting four-place knot would have to be one of five weak classes (13-17), which never failed in any search
title: Mutual selection at four places
